questions.question: Where should the patched connector live? I'll need a durable home for ~6-10 patch commits and a pinned version that the service runs from.

options.label: GitHub fork (Recommended)
options.description: Fork example/example-adapter to your account, clone to ~/git/example-adapter, work on a branch, service pins a commit. Generic fixes (agent-dir env, approvals) also offered upstream as PRs.

options.label: Local clone only
options.description: Same clone at ~/git/example-adapter with local commits, no remote fork. Simpler, but no off-machine backup and no upstream PRs.

options.label: Upstream PRs, then pin
options.description: Only send PRs upstream and wait for merges before deploying. Cleanest long-term, but blocks deployment on a single maintainer.

options.label: New example service (Recommended)
options.description: Start a separate local example service with its own configuration directory.

options.description: Reuse the existing example profile and preserve its settings.

options.description: Validate on localhost before replacing the synthetic example service.

questions.question: OpenCode's revert undoes both the conversation and the file changes since a message. OmO has session-tree branching but no file snapshots. What should revert do?

options.label: Conversation + files (Recommended)
options.description: Connector snapshots the git working tree before each user turn (dangling `git stash create` commit refs, no branch/stash pollution) and on revert restores files + branches the OmO session back to before that message; unrevert restores the post-turn snapshot. Non-git dirs: conversation-only with a visible notice.

options.label: Conversation only
options.description: Revert branches the OmO session back to before the message; files are left as they are, with a clear notice in the UI that file changes were not undone.

options.label: Keep disabled
options.description: Revert/unrevert stay unavailable and return a clear error; use fork instead.
